items.title: Somalia: Somali Army Chief, Turksom Commander Visit Baidoa for Security Talks
items.description: [Shabelle] Baidoa -- Somalia's army chief and the commander of Turkey's military training mission visited the southwestern city of Baidoa on Monday for talks with South West State leader Sheikh Aden Mohamed Nur (Madoobe) on strengthening security and expanding operations against Al-Shabaab.
items.titleIt: Somalia: Somali Army Chief, Turksom Commander Visit Baidoa for Security Talks

items.title: Libya: Somali Human Rights Commission Visits Detained Migrants in Eastern Libya
items.description: [Shabelle] Benghazi -- A delegation from Somalia's Independent Human Rights Commission visited a prison in eastern Libya on Monday, where dozens of Somali nationals are being held, as part of efforts to assess their conditions and strengthen cooperation with Libyan authorities.
items.titleIt: Libya: Somali Human Rights Commission Visits Detained Migrants in Eastern Libya

items.title: Somalia: Somalia, China Hold Talks On Defence Cooperation, AU Mission's Future
items.description: [Shabelle] Mogadishu -- Somalia's Defence Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi and Chinese Ambassador Wang Yu held talks in Mogadishu on Sunday focusing on defence cooperation, the campaign against Al-Shabaab and the future of the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM).
items.titleIt: Somalia: Somalia, China Hold Talks On Defence Cooperation, AU Mission's Future

items.title: Magnitude 5.5 quake jolts Egypt, triggering emergency response
items.description: A magnitude 5.5 earthquake struck near the Egyptian city of Suez early Monday, shaking buildings across Cairo and prompting authorities to activate emergency response plans. No casualties or significant damage were immediately reported.
items.titleIt: Magnitude 5.5 quake jolts Egypt, triggering emergency response

items.title: Egyptian PM announces investigation after Damietta port drone attack
items.description: Egypt's Prime Minister said Thursday that the country would now be examining the remains of a drone that attacked two vessels at the Egyptian port of Damietta on Wednesday.

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.
items.titleIt: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab

items.title: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran
items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.

items.title: Italy to propose Albania-style EU migrant hubs at post-Ceuta meeting
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, AUG 3 - Italy will propose the creation of EU migrant hubs outside the bloc along the lines of its centres in Albania at Tuesday's emergency meeting of European interior ministers following the arrival of thousands of migrants at the Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta last week, sources have said, confirming newspaper reports. Premier Giorgia Meloni's government has suspended arrangements regarding the Schengen agreement allowing for control-free movement between borders with Spain for a month following the events in Ceuta. items.titleIt: Italy to propose Albania-style EU migrant hubs at post-Ceuta meeting

items.title: Ethiopia: Hundreds Flee Ethiopia to War-Torn Sudan Following New Fighting in Tigray
items.description: [RFI] In Ethiopia, hundreds of people have started to flee to Sudan following Saturday's fighting, when clashes in Tigray pitted federal forces against rebels from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides accuse each other of seeking to trigger a new conflict.

items.title: 28% increase in passports issued by the Italian Consulate in Dubai
items.description: (ANSA) - ROMA, 28 LUG - The Consulate General of Italy in Dubai reports that in the first six months of 2026, it issued 1,340 passports, compared to 1,046 during the same period in 2025. This represents a 28% increase. “This increase,” explains the consulate, “did not occur in spite of the conflict, but rather because of the conflict.” Furthermore, the consular offices remained open throughout March to renew expiring passports and issue first passports to newborns. Read article...
